---
title: "Parsing model output"
guide-section: "Guides"
description: "How loads grounds records in the text, its options, and the issues it reports."
---

`cane.loads(output, text=..., variant=...)` reads a model's CANE output and finds each
record's place in the text. It never raises for problems in the output: everything that
could not be grounded comes back as a `ParseIssue`.

```{python}
import cane_format as cane

text = "Take aspirin with food. If pain persists, take aspirin again."
output = "Entities:\n`aspirin` is a DRUG\n`aspirin` is a DRUG\n`fever` is a ADR"
result = cane.loads(output, text=text, variant="base", labels={"DRUG", "ADR"})

[(e.label, e.spans) for e in result.entities], [str(i) for i in result.issues]
```

## Grounding: where a record lands

The parser grounds what the model wrote; it never judges whether a prediction is plausible.

- **Reading order.** Each record takes the earliest unused occurrence at or after the
  previous record's position, else the earliest unused one anywhere. Repeated mentions and
  nested entities land where a reader expects them. (On the CANE paper's model outputs this
  rule beat "earliest occurrence anywhere" in every case, including outputs grouped by
  label.)
- **Anchors** select the occurrence when there are several. If an anchor is not in the text,
  or does not contain its part, the record is reported as `anchor_not_found`.
- **Overlap never rejects.** Nested and overlapping entities are kept. A record that would
  repeat an earlier entity exactly is reported as `duplicate`.
- **Discontinuous parts** are grounded together: all parts or nothing, and parts may not
  overlap each other.

## Strict by default

Every leniency is an explicit switch, off by default, and the parser never tries a looser
setting on its own:

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `labels=` | Unknown labels keep the entity and add an `invalid_label` issue. |
| `match="normalized"` | Match after Unicode NFC normalisation. |
| `match="casefold"` | Match ignoring case. |
| `anchor_fallback=True` | Ground the bare part when its anchor is not found. |
| `strip_list_markers=True` | Accept lines starting with `- ` or `1. `. |
| `handles=True` | Records carry handles (`T1 …`), which become entity IDs. |
| `prefer_whole_words=True` | See below. |

All of them can be bundled in one `cane.ParseOptions`, which is also recorded on every
result as `result.settings`.

## Choosing an occurrence

Without anchors (Base, Disco), only the reading order decides, and the earliest occurrence
can be inside a longer word:

```{python}
text = "Maurice Tate against Northamptonshire at Northampton"
record = "`Northampton` is a LOC"
for prefer in (False, True):
    e = cane.loads(record, text=text, variant="base", prefer_whole_words=prefer).entities[0]
    print(f"prefer_whole_words={prefer}:", text[: e.start] + "[" + text[e.start : e.end] + "]" + text[e.end :])
```

`prefer_whole_words=True` tries occurrences that neither start nor end between two letters or
digits first. It only reorders candidates: an entity that occurs only inside a word is still
found, and in scripts written without spaces nothing changes.

## Issues

| Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `empty_output` | The output is empty: the generation probably failed. |
| `malformed_line` | The line is not a record of this variant. |
| `not_found` | A part does not occur in the text. |
| `anchor_not_found` | An anchor does not occur in the text, or does not contain its part. |
| `part_count_mismatch` | The number of anchors differs from the number of parts. |
| `unknown_handle` | A handle does not refer to an entity. |
| `invalid_label` | The label is not in `labels=`. |
| `invalid_span` | The parts cannot form a valid entity. |
| `duplicate` | The record repeats an earlier entity exactly. |

Each issue carries the raw line, its line number and the candidate spans that were
considered, so you can see why a line failed.
